# iAkauntan

> Accounting, CRM, HR and payroll, corporate secretarial and LHDN
> e-Invoice for Malaysian businesses. The HTTP surface is
> PostgREST over Postgres: every endpoint below is a function or a
> table in one database, and the authorization is that database's
> own row-level security rather than a layer in front of it.

Schema version `0582` (the highest applied migration).
662 functions and 329 readable tables, of which
254 functions only read.

Generated from the catalog by
`scripts/generate_api_description.py` and checked in CI, so this
file cannot drift from what the database will actually do.

**449 of 662 functions carry a `comment on
function`**, and those are the only ones described here in
words. The rest show their name, their arguments and their
types, which is what the catalog knows about them. A function
with no line of prose here is not a function that does nothing
surprising — it is one nobody has written down yet, and the
name is a worse guide than it looks.

## Before anything else

- **Base URL** `https://<project>.supabase.co/rest/v1`. Functions
  are `POST /rpc/<name>` with a JSON object of the named
  arguments; tables are `GET /<table>` with PostgREST's query
  syntax.
- **Two headers, both needed.** `apikey` is the project's anon
  key and grants nothing on its own. `Authorization: Bearer
  <token>` is the signed-in user, and it is what every policy
  reads. The service role key bypasses RLS entirely and belongs
  only in server-side code.
- **A company is an argument, not a session.** Most functions take
  `p_org_id` or `p_org`. A company you are not a member of is a
  42501, never an empty list.
- **A refusal is the rule speaking.** 42501 messages are written
  to be shown to a person. Do not paraphrase them; the guard
  knows why it said no and a paraphrase drifts.
- **Writes that must not repeat take a key.** See the idempotency
  overloads below.

## Idempotent writes

Four money writes have an overload whose first argument is
`p_idempotency_key`. A retry with the same key returns the first
call's answer; the same key with different arguments is refused
rather than quietly answered. The key has no default, because a
call that omits one merely-optional argument would otherwise
resolve to the unprotected original and return a plausible id.

- `create_contra`
- `create_deposit`
- `post_manual_journal`
- `record_pdc`

## Reachable without signing in

19 functions are granted to `anon`. Everything else
needs a user token.

- `corp_decline_with_link`
- `corp_open_signing_link`
- `corp_sign_with_link`
- `landing_page`
- `maintenance_notice`
- `may_sign_in_here`
- `open_customer_portal`
- `open_shared_document`
- `open_shared_ticket`
- `place_public_pos_order`
- `portal_document_token`
- `public_pos_menu`
- `public_pos_menu_modifiers`
- `reply_to_shared_ticket`
- `report_failed_sign_in`
- `shared_payment_options`
- `signup_reference`
- `site_pages`
- `workspace_by_host`

## The functions, by module

### accounting (12)

Refused unless the company has the `accounting` module switched on and the caller may use it.

- `archive_budget(p_id uuid)` *(writes)* — Puts a budget out of use.
- `budget_lines_for(p_budget uuid)`
- `budgets_list(p_org uuid)`
- `build_budget_from_actual(p_budget uuid, p_from_year uuid, p_uplift_percent numeric)` *(writes)* — Fills a draft budget from a previous year's actuals, period by period, with an optional uplift.
- `cash_forecast_detail(p_org uuid, p_from date, p_to date, p_use_history boolean)`
- `cash_forecast_items_list(p_org uuid)`
- `report_budget_vs_actual(p_budget uuid, p_from_period integer, p_to_period integer)` — What happened, what was supposed to, and whether the difference is good news.
- `report_cash_forecast(p_org uuid, p_weeks integer, p_use_history boolean)` — Thirteen weeks of cash by default, from what the bank holds now plus what is expected in and out.
- `retire_cash_forecast_item(p_id uuid)` *(writes)*
- `set_budget_lines(p_budget uuid, p_lines jsonb)` *(writes)* — Replaces a budget's lines wholesale and returns how many were written.
- `upsert_budget(p_id uuid, p_org uuid, p_year uuid, p_name text, p_department text, p_notes text)` *(writes)* — Creates or renames a budget for a financial year.
- `upsert_cash_forecast_item(p_id uuid, p_org uuid, p_direction text, p_description text, p_amount numeric, p_expected_on date, p_recurrence text, p_until date, p_notes text)` *(writes)* — Creates or edits one of the things only a person knows -- a payment expected or promised that no invoice or bill has yet recorded -- so the thirteen-week forecast can include it.

### crm (1)

Refused unless the company has the `crm` module switched on and the caller may use it.

- `report_pipeline_quote_mismatch(p_org uuid)` — Open deals whose figure no longer matches the quotation they are attached to.

### einvoice (2)

Refused unless the company has the `einvoice` module switched on and the caller may use it.

- `consolidate_pos_einvoices(p_org uuid, p_month date)` *(writes)* — Rolls a month of anonymous counter sales into one consolidated e-Invoice, due seven days after month end.
- `pos_einvoice_outstanding(p_org uuid)`

### fixed_assets (1)

Refused unless the company has the `fixed_assets` module switched on and the caller may use it.

- `report_uncapitalised_purchases(p_org uuid, p_as_at date)` — Posted bill lines coded to a fixed asset account with no asset in the register against them — the reconciliation an auditor opens with, which the data could not answer.

### forecasting (3)

Refused unless the company has the `forecasting` module switched on and the caller may use it.

- `create_po_from_suggestions(p_org uuid, p_lines jsonb, p_expected_date date, p_warehouse uuid)` *(writes)* — Turns the latest run for this location into one draft purchase order per supplier, ordering the stock into the place that is short of it.
- `forecast_suggestions(p_org uuid, p_warehouse uuid)` — What the latest run for this organization and location says to order, with the item and supplier named and any draft orders already raised netted off.
- `run_inventory_forecast(p_org uuid, p_warehouse uuid, p_as_of date)` *(writes)* — Forecasts every stocked item and records what it decided.

### inventory (26)

Refused unless the company has the `inventory` module switched on and the caller may use it.

- `bundle_availability(p_item uuid, p_warehouse uuid)`
- `bundle_margin(p_item uuid)`
- `cancel_landed_cost_run(p_run uuid)` *(writes)* — Cancels a landed-cost run -- freight, duty and handling being spread across the items on a shipment.
- `cancel_stock_transfer(p_id uuid)` *(writes)* — Cancels a transfer between warehouses.
- `delete_item_conversion(p_id uuid)` *(writes)*
- `delete_item_uom_pack(p_item uuid, p_uom text)` *(writes)*
- `item_bundle_for(p_item uuid)`
- `item_bundles_list(p_org uuid)`
- `item_conversion_outputs_for(p_conversion uuid)`
- `item_conversions_list(p_org uuid)`
- `item_uom_options(p_item uuid)`
- `item_variant_matrix(p_parent uuid)`
- `landed_cost_preview(p_run uuid)`
- `landed_cost_runs_list(p_org uuid, p_status text)`
- `post_landed_cost_run(p_run uuid)` *(writes)* — Puts a run's charges onto the cost of the goods that are still on the shelf, and takes the same money back off the accounts they were coded to.
- `receive_stock_transfer(p_id uuid, p_counts jsonb)` *(writes)*
- `run_item_conversion(p_conversion uuid, p_times numeric, p_warehouse uuid)` *(writes)* — Cuts one item up into others — a carcass into cuts, a drum into bottles — moving stock out of the source and into the outputs, with the source's cost split across them by `cost_share`.
- `send_stock_transfer(p_id uuid)` *(writes)*
- `set_item_weighed(p_item uuid, p_weighed boolean, p_plu text)` *(writes)* — Marks an item as sold by weight, with the PLU the scale prints.
- `stock_transfer_lines_for(p_transfer uuid)`
- `stock_transfers_list(p_org uuid, p_status app.stock_transfer_status)`
- `upsert_item_bundle(p_org uuid, p_item uuid, p_lines jsonb, p_notes text, p_active boolean)` *(writes)* — Defines what a bundle is made of.
- `upsert_item_conversion(p_id uuid, p_org uuid, p_code text, p_name text, p_item uuid, p_qty numeric, p_uom text, p_outputs jsonb, p_active boolean)` *(writes)* — Creates or edits a conversion -- one item broken down into several, a carcass into cuts, a drum into bottles.
- `upsert_item_uom_pack(p_item uuid, p_uom text, p_qty numeric)` *(writes)* — Says how many base units are in a pack -- a dozen, a case of twenty-four -- so an order in cases becomes a quantity in the books.
- `upsert_landed_cost_run(p_id uuid, p_org uuid, p_date date, p_bills jsonb, p_charges jsonb, p_notes text)` *(writes)* — Creates or edits a draft landed-cost run -- freight, duty and handling to be spread across the items on one or more bills.
- `upsert_stock_transfer(p_id uuid, p_org uuid, p_from uuid, p_to uuid, p_date date, p_lines jsonb, p_notes text)` *(writes)* — Creates or edits a draft transfer between two of this company's own warehouses.

### legal (2)

Refused unless the company has the `legal` module switched on and the caller may use it.

- `check_matter_conflict(p_org uuid, p_client uuid, p_opposing_party text)` — Both directions of a professional conflict: files where the firm acts for the proposed opposing party, and files where it has acted against the proposed client.
- `report_matters_over_agreed_fee(p_org uuid)` — Fixed-fee matters where billed plus unbilled time has passed the agreed fee.

### loyalty (11)

Refused unless the company has the `loyalty` module switched on and the caller may use it.

- `adjust_loyalty_points(p_account uuid, p_points integer, p_note text)` *(writes)* — Adds or removes points by hand and returns the new balance.
- `enrol_loyalty_member(p_contact uuid, p_card_no text)` *(writes)* — Puts a customer on the loyalty programme and returns the account.
- `expire_loyalty_points(p_org uuid)` *(writes)* — Zeroes the balance of every account dormant longer than the programme allows, and returns who lost what so somebody can look before it is believed.
- `loyalty_account_balance(p_contact uuid)`
- `loyalty_lookup(p_org uuid, p_query text)` — Finds a member from a card number, a phone or part of a name.
- `loyalty_member_tier(p_account uuid)` — Which tier an account is in, what it earned to get there, and how many points short of the next one — the sentence a cashier reads out.
- `loyalty_tiers_admin(p_org uuid)` — Every tier a company has, retired ones included, with how many members are actually sitting in each — which is how a shop finds out whether Gold means anything.
- `pos_sale_member(p_sale uuid)` — Who is on a bill, what they hold, what this bill is already redeeming and what paying it would earn.
- `redeem_loyalty_points(p_sale uuid, p_points integer)` *(writes)* — Spends points against a parked bill and returns what was applied.
- `retire_loyalty_tier(p_tier uuid)` *(writes)* — Switches a tier off.
- `upsert_loyalty_tier(p_program uuid, p_code text, p_name text, p_min_points integer, p_multiplier numeric, p_id uuid, p_is_active boolean)` *(writes)* — Creates or edits a tier on a loyalty programme -- the points at which it starts and what it multiplies earning by.

### memberships (5)

Refused unless the company has the `memberships` module switched on and the caller may use it.

- `cover_line_with_membership(p_line uuid, p_subscription uuid)` *(writes)*
- `membership_balance(p_subscription uuid)`
- `membership_billing_gaps(p_org uuid)` — Active memberships with no renewal schedule behind them.
- `set_membership_status(p_subscription uuid, p_status app.pos_membership_status)` *(writes)* — Changes a membership's status and returns what it became.
- `start_membership(p_sale uuid, p_membership uuid)` *(writes)*

### pos (124)

Refused unless the company has the `pos` module switched on and the caller may use it.

- `add_line_free_modifier(p_line uuid, p_group uuid, p_name text, p_price_delta numeric, p_quantity integer)` *(writes)* — Puts an answer nobody listed onto a line: a name and a price typed at the counter, snapshotted like any other.
- `add_line_modifier(p_line uuid, p_modifier uuid, p_quantity integer)` *(writes)* — Adds a choice to a rung line — no onions, extra cheese, medium rare — and returns the row.
- `add_pos_sale_line(p_sale uuid, p_item uuid, p_quantity numeric, p_price numeric, p_discount numeric, p_note text)` *(writes)* — Rings an item onto a bill and returns the new line.
- `apply_pos_coupon(p_sale uuid, p_code text)` *(writes)* — Attaches a voucher to a parked bill, refusing a code that does not qualify rather than attaching it inert.
- `assign_pos_delivery(p_delivery uuid, p_driver uuid)` *(writes)* — Puts a run on a driver's list, or moves it to another one.
- `begin_pos_count(p_shift uuid)` *(writes)* — Stops the till while the drawer is counted.
- `book_appointment(p_provider uuid, p_item uuid, p_starts_at timestamp with time zone, p_contact uuid, p_note text)` *(writes)*
- `bump_kitchen_ticket(p_ticket uuid, p_status app.pos_ticket_status)` *(writes)* — Moves a docket along the kitchen screen — new, cooking, ready, served — and stamps the time it reached that state.
- `check_in_booking(p_booking uuid, p_register uuid)` *(writes)*
- `claim_pos_sale(p_sale uuid, p_register uuid)` *(writes)* — Moves an open bill onto this till, register and shift together, so the drawer that takes the money is the drawer it counts against.
- `clear_pos_delivery(p_sale uuid)` *(writes)* — Takes the address and the fee back off a parked bill.
- `close_pos_shift(p_shift uuid, p_declared numeric, p_notes text)` *(writes)* — Counts a drawer out.
- `complete_kiosk_order(p_sale uuid, p_tender uuid, p_amount numeric, p_reference text)` *(writes)* — Takes payment for a self-service order, assigns the order number the customer watches for, and sends it to the kitchen if the outlet has one.
- `complete_pos_sale(p_sale uuid, p_tenders jsonb, p_contact uuid)` *(writes)* — Settles a parked sale: raises and posts the invoice, writes and posts a receipt for whatever was actually paid, records the tenders and awards the points.
- `delete_pos_recipe(p_recipe uuid)` *(writes)* — Removes the ingredient list behind a dish.
- `delete_pos_report(p_id uuid)` *(writes)* — Removes a saved report.
- `delete_scale_format(p_id uuid)` *(writes)*
- `ingest_offline_sales(p_register uuid, p_sales jsonb)` *(writes)* — Lands a batch of sales rung up with no signal.
- `item_modifier_group_ids(p_item uuid)` — Which questions a dish is currently sold with, retired ones included, so the editor shows what is actually attached.
- `item_modifier_options(p_item uuid)` — What can be asked about a dish: the questions attached to it, their rules, whether each takes an answer that is not listed, and the answers that are.
- `join_pos_queue(p_outlet uuid, p_party integer, p_name text, p_phone text, p_note text)` *(writes)* — Puts a party in the line and hands back their number, what they were told to expect, and how many are in front of them.
- `kiosk_order_board(p_outlet uuid)` — Order numbers still waiting, and whether they are being made or ready.
- `kitchen_display(p_station uuid)` — Open tickets at one station, oldest first — the only ordering a kitchen cares about is who has been waiting longest.
- `merge_pos_sales(p_into uuid, p_from uuid)` *(writes)* — Folds one parked bill into another and DESTROYS the emptied one, returning how many lines moved.
- `merge_pos_table(p_table uuid)` *(writes)* — Puts a split table back together.
- `move_pos_sale(p_sale uuid, p_table uuid)` *(writes)* — Moves a parked bill to another table, or to none when the table is null.
- `name_pos_sale_customer(p_sale uuid, p_contact uuid)` *(writes)* — Puts a customer on a parked sale, which is what loyalty redemption reads.
- `open_pos_sale(p_register uuid, p_contact uuid, p_client_uuid uuid)` *(writes)* — Opens a bill on a register and returns its id.
- `open_pos_shift(p_register uuid, p_float numeric, p_notes text)` *(writes)* — Opens a drawer with a counted float.
- `pos_day_board(p_org uuid, p_date date)` — One row per outlet for a trading day: bills, gross, cash and non-cash taken, average bill, what was written off — and how many bills are open right now, which is the one column on a different clock.
- `pos_day_sheet(p_outlet uuid, p_date date)` — One row per provider per booking for a day, and one row with nulls for a provider with an empty diary.
- `pos_delivery_board(p_outlet uuid)` — Every run at this outlet that has not landed, oldest first, with minutes waiting computed on the server so two devices cannot show two different boards.
- `pos_delivery_day(p_org uuid, p_date date)` — One day of delivering, per outlet: what went out, what came back, what the rides earned and how many were given away free.
- `pos_delivery_for(p_sale uuid)` — Where this bill is going, what the ride costs and who has it — with the shortfall sentence, so the till can say what is wrong while the customer is still on the phone.
- `pos_delivery_zones_admin(p_org uuid)`
- `pos_discount_summary(p_org uuid, p_from date, p_to date)` — What was discounted, by whom, on which day and in which shop.
- `pos_driver_runs(p_org uuid, p_date date)` — What each driver carried on one trading day, in Asia/Kuala_Lumpur.
- `pos_drivers_admin(p_org uuid)`
- `pos_even_split(p_sale uuid, p_ways integer)` — Equal shares of one bill that sum to it exactly, remainder on the first.
- `pos_floor_plan(p_outlet uuid)` — The dining room as it stands: every table, and every bill open on one.
- `pos_item_availability(p_outlet uuid)` — What the till should do with each dish that has a recipe: how many are left, and whether a stop or a schedule refuses it before the count does.
- `pos_item_portions(p_outlet uuid)` — How many more of each dish this outlet can make: the smallest number any required ingredient can still make, less what parked bills have already promised.
- `pos_line_modifier_gaps(p_sale uuid)` — Required choices nobody has made yet, per line.
- `pos_lookup_item(p_outlet uuid, p_code text)` — Resolves a scan or a typed search to sellable items.
- `pos_menu(p_outlet uuid)` — Everything an outlet can sell, with whether it is offered right now, why not, how many more the kitchen can make, and whether it is sold by weight.
- `pos_menu_links_admin(p_org uuid)`
- `pos_menu_schedules_admin(p_org uuid)` — Every schedule a company has written, with how many dishes are on it and whether it is open right now — which is the question somebody opens the screen to answer.
- `pos_modifier_groups_admin(p_org uuid)` — Every modifier group a company has, retired ones included, with how many answers it holds, how many dishes ask it, and whether it takes an answer that is not on the list.
- `pos_modifier_options_admin(p_group uuid)` — The answers to one modifier group, retired ones last, for the screen that edits them.
- `pos_offline_problems(p_org uuid)` — Sales a device took that the server could not accept.
- `pos_open_orders(p_outlet uuid)` — Every bill still open in an outlet, whichever till holds it.
- `pos_promotions_admin(p_org uuid)` — Every promotion a company has written, retired ones included, with how many bills used it and what it gave away.
- `pos_queue(p_outlet uuid)` — Everyone still in the line at this outlet today, in arrival order, with minutes waited computed on the server so two devices with different clocks cannot show two different queues.
- `pos_queue_day(p_org uuid, p_date date)` — What the line did on one day, per outlet.
- `pos_receipt_settings_for(p_outlet uuid)` — What this outlet prints, defaults included.
- `pos_receipt_text(p_sale uuid)` — The receipt as plain text, wrapped to the outlet's paper width.
- `pos_recent_sale(p_outlet uuid)` — The last bill this outlet settled.
- `pos_recipe_lines_for(p_recipe uuid)`
- `pos_recipe_requirement(p_item uuid, p_qty numeric)`
- `pos_recipes_list(p_org uuid)`
- `pos_report_headers(p_report uuid)`
- `pos_reports_list(p_org uuid)`
- `pos_sale_promotions_on(p_sale uuid)` — What is on this bill and what each took off, including coupons that currently qualify for nothing and the reason why.
- `pos_sales_by_channel(p_org uuid, p_from date, p_to date)` — Completed sales split by how the order arrived — how much of Friday was delivery, whether the dining room is worth the seats.
- `pos_scan_serial(p_line uuid, p_serial text)` *(writes)* — Scan one serial onto a till line, checked while the customer is still at the counter.
- `pos_stall_settlements_list(p_outlet uuid)`
- `pos_stall_takings(p_outlet uuid, p_from date, p_to date)` — What each stall sold over a period and what it is owed.
- `pos_stalls_list(p_outlet uuid)`
- `pos_station_routing(p_outlet uuid)` — Every sellable item, the counter it goes to, and which of the three rules decided that — the dish, its category, or the outlet default.
- `pos_stopped_items(p_outlet uuid)`
- `pos_table_by_code(p_outlet uuid, p_code text)` — The table a scanned card, QR sticker or typed code names, with how many bills are already open on it.
- `pos_unscan_serial(p_line uuid, p_serial text)` *(writes)* — Take a mis-scanned serial back off a till line.
- `pos_void_summary(p_org uuid, p_from date, p_to date)`
- `pos_voided_bills(p_org uuid, p_from date, p_to date)` — The bills written off in a period: what each came to, why, and who.
- `refresh_pos_sale_promotions(p_sale uuid)` *(writes)* — Re-runs every active promotion against a bill and returns the new total.
- `remove_line_modifier(p_line_modifier uuid)` *(writes)* — Takes a choice back off a line and re-prices the line.
- `remove_pos_sale_line(p_line uuid)` *(writes)* — Takes an unsent line off a parked bill.
- `remove_pos_sale_promotion(p_row uuid)` *(writes)* — Takes one promotion off a parked bill and returns the bill it was on.
- `request_einvoice_for_sale(p_sale uuid, p_contact uuid)` *(writes)* — The customer who asks after paying.
- `resume_pos_item(p_outlet uuid, p_item uuid)` *(writes)* — Puts a dish back on TODAY, undoing an 86.
- `resume_pos_shift(p_shift uuid)` *(writes)* — Puts a counting till back into service.
- `retire_kitchen_station(p_station uuid)` *(writes)* — Switches a counter off.
- `retire_pos_delivery_zone(p_id uuid)` *(writes)* — Switches a delivery area off.
- `retire_pos_driver(p_id uuid)` *(writes)* — Stands a driver down.
- `retire_pos_menu_link(p_id uuid)` *(writes)* — Switches off a public ordering link.
- `retire_pos_menu_schedule(p_schedule uuid)` *(writes)* — Switches a menu period off — breakfast, happy hour.
- `retire_pos_modifier(p_modifier uuid)` *(writes)* — Takes one answer off the menu without deleting it, so what was ordered on it stays answerable.
- `retire_pos_modifier_group(p_group uuid)` *(writes)* — Stops a question being asked, and says how many dishes that affects.
- `retire_pos_promotion(p_promo uuid)` *(writes)* — Switches an offer off.
- `route_category_to_station(p_category uuid, p_outlet uuid, p_station uuid)` *(writes)* — The same rule one level up: which counter makes everything in this category, in this outlet.
- `route_item_to_station(p_item uuid, p_outlet uuid, p_station uuid)` *(writes)* — Says which counter makes this dish IN THIS OUTLET — the same item in another shop keeps its own routing, which is why the table is not unique on item alone.
- `run_pos_report(p_report uuid, p_from date, p_to date)` — Runs a saved report and returns one row per group: the dimension values as text, the measures as numbers, both in the order the report declared.
- `scale_formats_list(p_org uuid)`
- `seat_table(p_register uuid, p_table uuid, p_covers integer)` *(writes)* — Seats a table from a register and returns the bill to work on, opening one only if the table has none.
- `send_order_to_kitchen(p_sale uuid)` *(writes)* — Prints the dockets: takes every line the kitchen has NOT yet seen, routes each to its station, and returns one row per docket made.
- `set_booking_status(p_booking uuid, p_status app.pos_booking_status, p_note text)` *(writes)* — Moves a table booking along.
- `set_item_modifier_groups(p_item uuid, p_groups uuid[])` *(writes)* — Sets which questions a dish is sold with, in the order they will be asked.
- `set_item_stall(p_item uuid, p_stall uuid)` *(writes)* — Puts an item on a stall in a food court, or takes it off with null.
- `set_outlet_channel(p_outlet uuid, p_channel app.pos_order_channel, p_is_active boolean, p_is_default boolean, p_sort_order integer)` *(writes)* — Configures one order channel for an outlet -- whether it is offered, whether it is the default, and where it sits in the list.
- `set_pos_delivery(p_sale uuid, p_line1 text, p_phone text, p_line2 text, p_city text, p_state text, p_postcode text, p_recipient text, p_notes text, p_promised timestamp with time zone, p_fee numeric)` *(writes)* — Takes or corrects the address on a parked bill, resolves the zone, derives the fee and puts the sale on the delivery channel.

- `post_purchase_payment(p_id uuid)` *(writes)* — Posts a payment to a supplier: money out of the bank, the payable discharged, and any exchange difference struck as its own line.
- `post_receipt(p_id uuid)` *(writes)* — Posts money received from a customer: bank debited net of charges, bank charges to their own account, receivable credited, and any exchange movement between the invoice and the receipt struck as its own line.
- `post_sales_document(p_id uuid)` *(writes)* — Posts an invoice, credit note, debit note or refund note to the ledger.
- `post_stock_adjustment(p_id uuid)` *(writes)* — Posts a stock take or write-off at current average cost, line by line, skipping lines where the count agreed.
- `post_withholding(p_id uuid)` *(writes)* — Posts a withholding certificate: the control account comes down and the amount becomes owed to the Inland Revenue Board.
- `prepare_einvoice(p_sales_document_id uuid)` *(writes)* — Snapshots a posted sales document into MyInvois e-Invoice form and queues it for submission.
- `property_statutory_due(p_org_id uuid, p_within_days integer)`
- `public_pos_menu(p_token text)` — The menu behind one published link.
- `public_pos_menu_modifiers(p_token text, p_item uuid)` — The option groups for one item on a QR menu, for a customer holding a phone at a table.
- `quote_opportunity(p_opportunity uuid, p_valid_until date, p_description text)` *(writes)* — Raises a quotation from a deal and links the two.
- `raise_rent_invoices(p_site_id uuid, p_period_from date, p_period_to date, p_due_date date)` *(writes)* — Invoices every active tenancy at a site for a period, POSTS each invoice, and returns the run.
- `raise_strata_charges(p_scheme_id uuid, p_period_from date, p_period_to date, p_due_date date)` *(writes)* — Charges every parcel in a scheme for a period — maintenance at the rate per share unit, plus the sinking fund contribution as a second line — POSTS each invoice, and returns the run.
- `receive_client_money(p_matter uuid, p_amount numeric, p_date date, p_description text, p_reference text, p_payment_mode text)` *(writes)* — Money received from a client to hold on account for a matter.

- `record_pdc(p_org uuid, p_direction text, p_contact uuid, p_cheque_no text, p_cheque_date date, p_amount numeric, p_documents jsonb, p_bank uuid, p_bank_name text, p_received date, p_notes text)` *(writes)* — Puts a post-dated cheque in the register and takes the document it settles off the aged listing, without touching the bank balance.
- `record_pdc(p_org uuid, p_direction text, p_contact uuid, p_cheque_no text, p_cheque_date date, p_amount numeric, p_documents jsonb, p_bank uuid, p_bank_name text, p_received date, p_notes text, p_idempotency_key text)` *(writes)*

## Tables

Read with `GET /<table>`. Row-level security decides which rows
come back, so an empty list is a real answer and not an error.
Writing through the table endpoints is not described here: the
functions above carry the business rules, and an INSERT that
bypasses them is refused by a policy or leaves the books
inconsistent.

- `access_permissions`
- `access_type_modules`
- `access_types`
- `accounts`
- `activities`
- `ai_conversations`
